q: The circle criterion for absolute stability of a feedback system with nonlinearity φ ∈ [k₁, k₂] (sector condition) states that stability holds if the Nyquist plot of G(jω) does not intersect or encircle the disk D(k₁,k₂) centered at (−(k₁+k₂)/(2k₁k₂), 0). This is equivalent to:
opts: The loop transfer function G(s) maps the boundary of D(k₁,k₂) into the left half-plane (Nyquist criterion on the modified plant)
The eigenvalues of G(0) being negative
exp: Circle criterion: system is absolutely stable for φ ∈ [k₁,k₂] iff the Nyquist plot of G(jω) lies entirely outside (or entirely inside) the critical disk D(k₁,k₂). This is a graphical criterion generalizing the Nyquist criterion for linear stability. It is implied by the Popov criterion in many cases.
